answer: To deter Sybil attacks in an agent swarm monitoring an opal quarry across a mountain ridge, nodes authenticate peers via clock-skew fingerprinting of each radio's quartz crystal oscillator. Because each hardware oscillator produces a unique drift profile, an adversary cannot virtualize multiple identities on one machine, imposing discrete hardware procurement costs. However, ambient thermal swings alter resonant frequencies, causing legitimate agents to be falsely rejected.
